# Native Windows type-library evidence

Captured on `Windows` (Tiny11) on 2026-10-23. These files were generated by
`tools/oracle_probe/typelib_fixture_probe.cpp` calling native Windows Automation
interfaces. No external runtime implementation generates the files or expectations.

Authoritative API contracts:
- [CreateTypeLib2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/oleauto/nf-oleauto-createtypelib2)
- [ICreateTypeInfo::AddFuncDesc](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/oaidl/nf-oaidl-icreatetypeinfo-addfuncdesc)
- [LoadTypeLibEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/oleauto/nf-oleauto-loadtypelibex)

The on-disk record schema is measured from these generated files. The API
pages describe the creation and inspection contracts, not the binary schema.
Semantic observations are checked in beside the probe as
`typelib_fixture_probe.x86.expected` and `typelib_fixture_probe.x64.expected`.

## Reproduction

Cross-compile the probe with MinGW GCC/G++ 15.2.0:

```sh
i686-w64-mingw32-g++ -O2 -static tools/oracle_probe/typelib_fixture_probe.cpp -loleaut32 -lole32 -luuid -o /tmp/typelib-fixture-x86.exe
x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ -O2 -static tools/oracle_probe/typelib_fixture_probe.cpp -loleaut32 -lole32 -luuid -o /tmp/typelib-fixture-x64.exe
```

Copy the executables to a dedicated directory on `Windows`, run each there,
and capture stdout separately. Both runs generate all twenty `.tlb` files;
copy the files back and compare their checksums before replacing fixtures.
An executable also accepts one filename to inspect an existing fixture.

| Variant | Controlled change from variant 0 |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Named interface; BSTR input and LONG pointer return parameter |
| 1 | Library GUID, version, locale and restricted flag |
| 2 | Type GUID, version and flags |
| 3 | Member ID and property-get invocation kind |
| 4 | Second method and nonzero vtable offset |
| 5 | Local interface inheritance |
| 6 | Scalar VARTYPEs and SAFEARRAY(BSTR) |
| 7 | Local enum referenced by a parameter |
| 8 | Coclass with implemented interface |
| 9 | Help-string DLL and its extra header word |

Each variant exists for SYS_WIN32 and SYS_WIN64. The decoder regression in
`tests/winapi/oleaut32/test_typelib.cpp` compares library/type/function/parameter
summaries with native observations for matching file and reader bitness. It
also rejects damaged offsets, record lengths and descriptor cycles.

## Scope and limitations

The reader produces a summary, not a complete TYPEDESC graph or Automation
implementation. Pointer types are flattened to values in that existing summary
interface. Imported references remain unresolved VT_USERDEFINED references.
Alias targets, C arrays, default values, full variable descriptions and imported
library resolution are not established by this corpus. Cross-bitness native
reads rescale some sizes; the decoder exposes file-target sizes and the existing
public API layer still needs separate coverage for that transformation.
The passing tests must not be described as full ITypeInfo parity.
